property_summary: Only calls to withdraw originating from the contract's Owner address can succeed (not revert).
The test asserts that calling c.withdraw() reverts exactly when the supplied caller address is not equal to c.Owner().
Withdraw reverts exactly when the provided caller address is not equal to the contract's Owner.
The test asserts that calling c.withdraw() reverts exactly when the supplied caller address is not equal to c.Owner().

For any caller and any sequence of calls, only the Owner can change contract balance by calling withdraw (i.e., calling withdraw does not allow non-Owner callers to move the contract's ETH away from the contract except to Owner under Owner control); the mutant removing the require allows a non-Owner caller to trigger withdraw and thus changes address(c).balance compared to the reference for some inputs.

For all callers and inputs, calling Command(...) that forwards a failing external call cannot change address(c).balance in the reference because only Owner can withdraw later; the mutant (which removes the withdraw-owner check) allows a non-Owner-invoked withdraw to empty the contract and thus can make address(c).balance decrease for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any provided target callee address that REVERTS when called, executing Command(target, data) as that caller must NOT change the contract's ETH balance in the reference (because only Owner can withdraw later), whereas the mutant (which removed the Owner check in withdraw) can allow a non-Owner caller to later empty the contract via withdraw and thus make address(c).balance decrease for some inputs.

For any caller and any sequence, after calling Command(target,data) the contract's Owner remains the only address able to reduce address(c).balance by invoking withdraw; the mutant (which removes the require in withdraw) allows a non-Owner caller to cause address(c).balance to drop for some fuzzed inputs.

For every caller and inputs, calling Command(...) must never make a subsequent non-Owner invocation of withdraw succeed in removing contract balance (i.e., only Owner can successfully withdraw); the mutant removes the Owner check and thus allows some non-Owner to withdraw and change address(c).balance.
After sending some ETH into c by calling payable functions, calling withdraw does not revert (i.e., succeeds) whenever the caller is the Owner and the contract has a positive prior balance.
For the owner caller, withdraw never reverts regardless of the contract balance (it may succeed even when balance is zero).
If caller is Owner then withdraw should not revert (i.e., succeeds) even when contract balance is zero.
When called by the Owner, withdraw should never revert (i.e., always succeed) regardless of c's balance.
If withdraw is called by the Owner and the contract's balance is zero, the call should not revert (i.e., original allows withdrawing with zero balance; mutant adds a require that makes it revert).

For any caller and any calldata/value forwarded via Command to a callee that reverts, the reference contract C will still allow Owner to withdraw the full contract balance afterward, but the mutant (which requires address(this).balance>0 before withdraw) can be put into a state where withdraw reverts (fails) after such an interaction, breaking that invariant for some inputs.

For any fuzzed nonzero deposit amount and any callee address, after the owner calls Command forwarding that deposit to a callee that REVERTS, the reference contract C still lets the owner withdraw the contract balance (withdraw succeeds / address(c).balance == 0 after withdraw); the mutant that adds require(address(this).balance > 0) can block withdraw when the forwarded call caused the contract balance to become zero (so withdraw reverts) — the test drives Command to a reverting callee and checks owner can always withdraw on the reference.

For any address and calldata, if the Owner sends ETH through Command to a callee that forwards the ETH out (succeeds), the reference contract always lets Owner withdraw remaining balance (i.e., after such Command the Owner can call withdraw successfully / address(c).balance == 0), while the mutant that requires address(this).balance > 0 before withdraw can be made to revert when the callee drains the forwarded value leaving balance zero.

For any fuzzed deposit amount and a callee that may revert, if the owner calls Command forwarding some value and afterwards attempts withdraw, the reference contract always allows withdraw to succeed (owner can extract remaining balance / address(c).balance becomes 0), while the mutant that requires address(this).balance > 0 can be made to have withdraw revert when the forwarded call drains or leaves balance zero — so the property: after a Command call that forwards value to a callee which reverts, the owner can still successfully call withdraw on the reference for every admissible input, but the mutant fails for some input.

For any fuzzed deposit amount and any callee that reverts when called, if the Owner calls Command forwarding that deposit, the reference contract C will always allow Owner to subsequently withdraw (withdraw succeeds and leaves address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant that requires address(this).balance > 0 can have withdraw revert when the forwarded call causes the contract balance to be zero.

For any caller who is the Owner, calling withdraw transfers the entire contract balance to the Owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and Owner's balance increases); the mutant sends the funds to msg.sender instead and thus can send funds to a different recipient, violating that the contract balance becomes 0 and Owner receives the funds for some inputs.

For every admissible caller and deposit amount, after Owner calls withdraw the contract balance becomes zero (Owner receives funds); the mutant can break this because it sends funds to msg.sender (which may not be Owner) causing the contract to not transfer funds to Owner.

For any caller who is the Owner and any pre-funded contract balance, calling withdraw always makes the contract balance zero (all funds are transferred out); the mutant can fail this because it transfers to msg.sender which (even when equal to Owner) still results in funds leaving the contract but the adversarial scenario where Owner is a contract that rejects receiving funds can cause the mutant to differ — the reference still succeeds because transfer to Owner uses a payable address that will revert if Owner cannot receive, preserving semantics, while the mutant sending to msg.sender can bypass/alter that behavior for some inputs (we target a case where Owner is a contract that reverts on receive).

For every caller and deposit, if Owner is a contract that reverts on receiving Ether, then when Owner (the Owner address) calls withdraw the reference C will revert (because it attempts to transfer to Owner) while the mutant that sends to msg.sender may succeed when msg.sender is an EOA — thus reference always reverts in this scenario but the mutant does not for some inputs.

For every caller who is Owner (including when Owner is a contract that rejects payments), calling withdraw either (A) transfers the contract balance to the Owner (succeeds and leaves address(c).balance == 0) or (B) reverts if Owner cannot receive funds; the buggy mutant can instead send funds to msg.sender and thus can succeed when Owner would have caused a revert — so the property: when Owner is a contract that rejects Ether, withdraw called by Owner must revert (reference: always reverts; mutant: may succeed).

For any caller who is the Owner and any contract balance, invoking withdraw transfers the contract's entire balance to Owner (so contract balance becomes zero); the mutant that sends only half can leave a non-zero balance and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller that is the Owner and for any nonzero contract balance funded by an arbitrary payer, calling withdraw empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers only half can leave a positive balance for some inputs.

For any nonzero ether balance in C and when Owner calls withdraw, the reference empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0) while the mutant that transfers only half can leave a positive remaining balance (thus violating the emptiness rule for some inputs).

For any nonzero contract balance and when Owner calls withdraw, the reference transfers the entire contract balance to Owner (so Owner's balance increases by address(c).balance), whereas the mutant transfers only half and thus Owner's received amount can be strictly less than the previous contract balance.

For any nonzero deposit amount sent by any payer to C and then withdrawn by Owner, the reference empties C (address(c).balance == 0) after withdraw; the mutant that transfers only half can leave a nonzero remaining balance for some deposits, violating this emptiness property.
If the Owner calls Command with a nonzero msg.value, the contract's balance decreases by that msg.value after the call (i.e., the call forwards the sent ether); otherwise balance unchanged.
